selection: Algerian-born French literary fiction after English humor and satire; no influence claim.

sources.use: French national library biography confirms birth on November 7, 1913 in Mondovi, Algeria, death on January 4, 1960, and L’Étranger publication in 1942.

Specialist society bibliography confirms all four original fiction-book years and identifies A Happy Death as written 1936–1938 but published in 1971, and The First Man as unfinished and published in 1994.
University-hosted digital library independently records the four French books as 1942, 1947, 1956 and 1957, and distinguishes posthumous 1971 and 1994 editions.
National library catalogue corroborates the 1957 Gallimard Exile and the Kingdom volume as nouvelles (short stories).

verifiedScope.proxy: Lifetime original-French prose-fiction book-publication span, from The Stranger to Exile and the Kingdom, used as a publishing proxy rather than a full-career span or a claim of uninterrupted writing. The four markers cover his three lifetime novels and his short-story collection, using first French book years, not composition, periodical appearances, later editions or English translations; English titles are supplied for readability. The Stranger (also translated as The Outsider), The Plague and The Fall appeared in French in 1942, 1947 and 1956; Exile and the Kingdom followed in 1957. A Happy Death was written in 1936–1938 but first published posthumously in 1971, and the unfinished The First Man appeared in 1994; neither extends this lifetime bar. Essays, journalism, plays, adaptations, notebooks and correspondence are outside this prose-fiction-book scope.
